claim: WFP reported on 16 March 2021 that monitored food prices were rising after the coup: palm oil in peri-urban Yangon was up 20% since early February, rice in peri-urban Yangon and Mandalay up 4% from the last week of February, and fuel prices about 15% higher nationwide since 1 February.
limitations: Market monitoring covered many locations but not every household or market; price increases varied sharply by township.

claim: WFP found much larger local food-price increases in some areas, including rice increases of 20-35% in Bhamo and Putao and higher cooking-oil/pulse prices in parts of Rakhine, showing that national averages could conceal local stress.
limitations: Regional market prices are not equivalent to household food insecurity; affordability depends on income and access.

claim: WFP reported near paralysis of the banking sector, slowing remittances and widespread cash-availability limits in March 2021, compounding food and fuel pressures.
limitations: Describes access constraints, not a complete measurement of all formal and informal finance channels.

claim: WFP reported building contingency food stocks to preserve assistance to more than 360,000 people, mainly internally displaced people in camps, if cash or market supply became constrained.
limitations: Prepared assistance is a counter-pressure; it does not prove needs were fully met or that broader instability was reduced.

claim: By 22 April 2021 WFP warned that pre-existing poverty, COVID-19 and the political crisis were combining to increase hunger; it projected up to 3.4 million additional people could become hungry within six months and described households skipping meals, eating less nutritious food and taking on debt.
limitations: The 3.4 million figure is a forward estimate, not an observed count at publication time; household examples are not a population denominator.

claim: WFP announced a scale-up targeting up to 2 million vulnerable people in poor urban townships and displacement-affected areas while continuing assistance to people affected by long-running conflict.
limitations: Targeting and program scale do not establish successful coverage of every intended beneficiary.

claim: UNHCR's 2021 global reporting recorded about 430,000 people newly internally displaced after the 1 February takeover and 671,000 IDPs at year end, alongside displacement into neighboring countries.
limitations: Year-end synthesis is not admissible for early-2021 cutoffs; contemporaneous monthly displacement products should be used for earlier snapshots.

claim: UNHCR published a displacement overview dated 21 June 2021, demonstrating that contemporaneous geospatial displacement monitoring existed during the pilot period and can be used instead of later retrospective totals for June cutoffs.
limitations: This row establishes an admissible sensor/document, not a numeric displacement claim until the underlying map/data are extracted and validated.

claim: World Bank's Myanmar COVID-19 High-Frequency Phone Survey collected six rounds between May 2020 and 3 February 2021 covering demographics, employment, agriculture, remittances, consumption, food insecurity, health and education, providing a pre-coup baseline across multiple latent-pressure domains.
limitations: Survey observations pre-date the coup, but the metadata page was produced in July 2021; whether individual underlying outputs were publicly observable at each early cutoff must be checked before historical use.
